name: Razor Hill Watchtower
summary: Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar from the Razor Hill Watchtower. From the red stone bluffs, he keeps watch over the plains and coast, guarding the settlement below.

sections.title: Eyes Over Durotar
sections.body: Above Razor Hill, the watchtower looks out across the settlement and the surrounding canyons. Thick timber and iron hold the outpost firm. Durotar faces Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders across the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists in nearby crags. From the ridgeline, a lookout can spot warbands, smoke signals, and incursions before they reach the gates.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Razor Hill Watchtower?
faq.answer: The Razor Hill Watchtower is the main lookout for Razor Hill and central Durotar. From its height, scouts watch the trails for hostile beasts and troop movements from nearby Alliance camps or centaur raiding parties.
Furl Scornbrow, an aging orc, watches for invaders and sounds his signal horn when needed. As Durotar has grown more settled, he has also taken to making bags for young adventurers.

faq.q: What threats can be seen from up here?
faq.answer: Scouts watch for aggressive quilboar of the Razormane tribes, human infiltrators from Tiragarde Keep along the eastern coast, and wild beasts in the dry valleys.

angles.text: For young warriors and scouts leaving the Valley of Trials, the watchtower is a reassuring sign of the fledgling Horde’s safety and strength.
As a hunter, you can use the watchtower’s high, open vantage point to track quarry and watch the beasts move across Durotar.
